draft.change: Add the pointed Syriac name אָרָמ and document its correspondence to Hebrew רָם in this genealogy.
draft.definition: The Syriac personal name Aram, borne here by Hezron’s son Ram.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:3 places Aram after Hezron in the genealogy. Ruth 4:18–19 gives the same succession from Perez through Hezron to Ram.

evidence.note: חֵצרֻונ אַולֵדֿ לָארָמ means “Hezron fathered Aram.”
Perez fathers Hezron, and Hezron fathers רָם.

article.name: אָרָמ
article.summary: The Peshitta names Hezron’s son אָרָמ in Matthew’s genealogy. Ruth calls him רָם in the Hebrew genealogy.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: In אָרָמ אַולֵדֿ לעַמִינָדָֿבֿ, Aram is the father of Amminadab. The genealogy continues from verse 3, where Aram is named as Hezron’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.

analysis.evidence: In אָרָמ אַולֵדֿ לעַמִינָדָֿבֿ, Aram is the subject and ל marks Amminadab as the object. Amminadab then becomes the subject of the same verb in the next father–son link.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: אָרָמ אַולֵדֿ לעַמִינָדָֿבֿ means “Ram fathered Amminadab.” The next clause repeats the name without ל as the subject of “fathered Nahshon,” confirming the bearer.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Amminadab, son of Ram and father of Nahshon.

analysis.evidence: The preceding clause names Amminadab as Aram’s son. The marked occurrence begins the next clause, עַמִינָדָֿבֿ אַולֵדֿ לנַחשָונ, “Amminadab fathered Nahshon.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Amminadab, son of Aram and father of Nahshon.

analysis.evidence: In עַמִינָדָֿבֿ אַולֵדֿ לנַחשָונ, Amminadab is the subject and ל־ marks Nahshon as the object. The clause records that Amminadab fathered Nahshon.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: In עַמִינָדָֿבֿ אַולֵדֿ לנַחשָונ, Amminadab fathers Nahshon. The next clause repeats the name without ל as its subject and says that Nahshon fathered Salmon. Ruth 4:20 gives the same succession.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ, “fathered.”
analysis.sense: Nahshon, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon.

analysis.evidence: Amminadab fathers Nahshon in the preceding clause. The marked occurrence begins the next clause, נַחשֻונ אַולֵדֿ לסַלמָונ, “Nahshon fathered Salmon.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, unprefixed and unsuffixed, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Nahshon, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon.

analysis.evidence: In נַחשֻונ אַולֵדֿ לסַלמָונ, Nahshon is the subject and the prefixed ל marks Salmon as the object. The verb states that Nahshon fathered Salmon.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix
